request: the owner, 2026-10-02, verbatim: "make an ursuluna cave at 1504 164 1414, dig a solid size caev for a large ursuluna, have teddiursa spawn on the outskirt and have an npc one players can talk to"

site.mouth_why: the owner's coordinate. tools/ground.py reads y162 there (heightmap 162.19), so the owner's y164 is a standing eye-line two blocks up, not the floor: the cave floor is the ground at the mouth, and a player walks in without a step. Highwire's nearest building (gym3_house_03, (1661, 1410)) is 157 blocks east; Route 3 ends at Highwire's centre (1688, 1410) coming up from the south-east, and Route 4 leaves it eastward.
site.axis_why: into the hill. The mouth sits on the south-east foot of a ridge that climbs north-west to y200 at (1450, 1350) and y217 at (1432, 1294) (tools/ground.py, sampled every 6 blocks). Due west the ground only reaches y174 before falling again, and due north y174: neither covers a chamber. North-west it rises 162 -> 180 in 25 blocks and to y194 over the chamber, so the chamber is under 13+ blocks of hill. The mouth therefore opens to the south-east, 45 degrees off the line to Highwire (due east), facing the last stretch of Route 3.

cave.margin_why: the legendary chambers' shell_margin (data/legendaries.json defaults, WATER_BUILD_PLAN 4.5 audit 1): at least 4 blocks of rock round every void past the mouth, guaranteed by construction because the shell is filled solid before the void is cut.
cave.keep_natural_top_why: the shell never writes into the top two blocks of any column, so the grass and the dirt under it stay the terrain's own and the hill's surface is never raised or re-skinned.
cave.open_mouth_until_why: the mouth is a cut and then an overhang, not a door. The passage's top block is y170 and tools/ground.py reads the crown line (s:y) 0:162 8:167 13:170 14:171 17:173 20:175 22:177: so s 0-13 is a cut open to the sky, the roof begins at s 14 (the arch, about (1494, 1404)), and its roof is the hillside's own grass and dirt until the ground stands margin + 1 over it at s 20. The slope also falls away sideways there: the audit's seal check, which looks margin blocks in every direction and not only up, first holds at s 22 (at 21 one block of open air at (1484, 174, 1404) is within 4 of the passage). 22 is that measured boundary, not a padded one; past it every carved block has margin + 1 blocks of ground over it and margin blocks of rock round it.

passage.why: a half-elliptical bore 9 wide at the floor and 8 high at the crown, level at the mouth's ground (y162) all the way in: wide and tall enough that the opening reads as a bear's den from the slope below, and level so nothing has to be climbed. It overlaps the chamber by 3 blocks so the two join without a lip.

chamber.why: a half-ellipsoid hall 39 blocks long, 29 wide and 17 high over a flat floor, centred 60 blocks in. Sized from the model, not guessed: the Ursaluna stands 8 by 8 by at most 10.3 blocks at scale 2 (ursaluna.model below), so the den end of the hall, 11 blocks from the centre where the bear lies, still has 23 blocks of width at the floor and 14 of height over it (tools/ursaluna_cave.py --report): the bear fills the den without touching it, and the hall in front is twice its size again.

den.why: where the den floor (podzol) begins, 6 blocks before the bear: the line the barrier curtain's far face used to stand on. There is NO curtain any more (the owner, 2026-10-02, after walking the den on staging: "i dont like the invisible blocks around the ursuluna"; offered three options, they chose "Wake it as a boss fight": no wall, the bear wakes and fights when you get close). The hall is open from the mouth to the bear; what protected the sleeping bear is now the wake (ursaluna.wake), which fires before a player on foot can reach it.

cave.lanterns_why: hanging lanterns under the roof (docs/STATE.md, 'Places are lit as towns': lanterns, never light blocks), each [s, p]: s along the axis from the mouth, p across it. Three down the passage (the first just inside the arch: s 0-13 is an open cut with no roof to hang from), five over the hall, one in the den over the bear so it is seen.
cave.blocks_why: vanilla only, and none of them is a spawn-conditioning block in data/spawn_blocks.json, so the cave adds no pack spawns. BUILD_PALETTE.md lists the decoration providers and names no cave stone; the shell is the stone the hill is made of.

ursaluna.level_why: THE FIGHT'S level, and only the fight's: since the owner's boss rules of 2026-10-02 the catch is gated by badges (ursaluna.catch), not by this number. The den is in the_tri_peaks, band 20-28, tier 3 (data/spawns.json subregions, since the encounter rebuild of 2026-10-02), reached from Highwire (gym 3, data/towns.json gym3_town) at the end of Route 3, whose last trainer's top level is 27 (data/trainers.json route_03_trainer_05: 25, 26, 27). 30 is two over the band and Lt. Surge's ace (gym_ace_levels[2], data/trainers.json generation_contract): a gym-sized fight for a party on that band, which can switch six times against one bear. 30 is also where Teddiursa evolves (Cobblemon 1.8.0 species data), so the mother stands a stage and a level above every cub on the slope. The jar's learnset puts slash at 22, playnice at 25 and playrough at 29 and headlongrush only at 1 (ursaluna.json); which four moves Cobblemon gives a level-30 spawn is NOT verified. The level cap (data/level_cap.json, strictly over the thrower's RCT cap) no longer decides the catch: every thrower the badge gate lets through is on a cap of 41 or more (ursaluna.catch.why), far over 30. Gating the catch by level instead was rejected: it needs the bear at 41 or more against a 20-28 band.
ursaluna.yaw_why: facing south-east, back along the axis toward the mouth and the visitor: Minecraft yaw 0 faces +z, -90 faces +x, so -45 faces (+x, +z).
ursaluna.scale_why: 'large' is the scale_modifier property: Cobblemon 1.8.0's PokemonProperties parses scale_modifier= (strings in PokemonProperties and PokemonProperties$Companion, Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar) and Pokemon.getEffectiveScale returns the scale modifier for a non-alpha Pokemon past baby age (javap of Pokemon.class). It is saved as ScaleModifier, so a restart keeps it. NOT alpha=true, which also exists: getAlphaScaleMultiplier fixes an alpha's scale at 1.1 + 0.8 * 0.5^max(hitbox) = 1.3 for Ursaluna's 2.0 hitbox and ignores scale_modifier, and an alpha brings the alpha battle boost and drops, which are balance, not size. NEEDS AN IN-GAME CHECK: that the summoned bear is twice normal size (the property is applied after the random intrinsic scale is rolled, which the bytecode suggests but no run has shown).
ursaluna.nbt_why: the DORMANT flags: the sleeping Celebi's exactly (data/sapling_celebi.json nbt, EXP-023: each proved to hold across a restart). Ursaluna's own poser has a SLEEP pose (posers/0901_ursaluna/ursaluna.json 'sleep', animation.ursaluna.sleep), so the pose has something to play. Merged by ursaluna_cave/dress whenever a fresh bear is installed, which also sets the awake score back to 0.
ursaluna.encounter_why: the owner, 2026-10-02, choosing among three options for the barrier: "Wake it as a boss fight" - no wall: the bear wakes and fights when you get close, as the den's set-piece encounter; its level set against the area's 20-28 band. Built on the sleeping Celebi's wake (docs/mechanics/CELEBI_WAKE.md, data/sapling_celebi.json wake): a state check on the keeper's own loop, an awake score the keeper stands down on, and the Celebi's AWAKE merge. Where the den differs: no item and no badge gate (the owner asked for 'when you get close'), and the bear is woken in its own pack rather than by tools/legendaries.py. Then the boss rules, the owner, 2026-10-02, verbatim: "Den boss: returns after it is beaten, no badge to wake it, catchable only late. A boss that stays dead is an event; one that returns is a place." So it is NOT one encounter per server: knocked out, caught or killed, it comes back asleep on its spot after ursaluna.returns.cooldown_ticks, and only a thrower with ursaluna.catch.gate_flags can catch it.

keeper.why: the Celebi keeper's shape (tools/sapling_celebi.py celebi/keep): every 2 s while a player is within 48 blocks of the den, AND ONLY WHILE IT SLEEPS, remove a second tagged bear if a load race made one and put it back on its spot if anything moved it, then look for the wake. Awake, near does nothing at all: a keeper that teleports a woken bear home every 40 ticks would drag it through the fight (docs/mechanics/CELEBI_WAKE.md 4, the keeper fault). Unlike the Celebi's, this keeper also SUMMONS, for the return (ursaluna.returns): through a macro line, which EXP-046 saw spawn at a fresh boot and put a killed worker back from its keeper (a plain spawnpokemonat line parsed at server start spawns nothing until a /reload). Every pass on which the den spot is loaded runs ursaluna_cave/track, whoever is near.

wake.status: built 2026-10-02, not run in game: experiments/EXP-049-ursaluna-wake
wake.trigger_why: the Celebi's mechanism (docs/mechanics/CELEBI_WAKE.md 1): a STATE CHECK inside the keeper's own 40-tick loop, never an advancement, so it cannot be burned and costs one selector per 40 ticks only while a player is within the keeper's 48 blocks. The Celebi's selector carries a gate and a held item; the den's carries neither, because the owner asked for a bear that wakes when you get close. Spectators are excluded.
wake.radius_why: measured from the bear's spot. The hall begins 30 blocks in front of the bear (chamber centre 60 - half_length 19 = s 41; the bear is at s 71), so a player in the passage, or standing at the hall's threshold, does not wake it: it wakes once they are a few steps into the hall, with the whole bear in front of them. Nothing outside the cave is within 24 of it either: the nearest ground a player can stand on outside the cave is 29.9 blocks from the bear's spot, and the nearest reachable block before the hall 30.4 (tools/ursaluna_cave_audit.py notes, 2026-10-02; the hill stands at y198 over the den and the bear's feet are at y163), so nobody wakes it from the passage or through the rock. tools/ursaluna_cave_audit.py checks both from the heightmap, and that no air a player can reach is within reach + 1 of the bear's hitbox without being inside this radius.
wake.gate_why: none (the owner, 2026-10-02: "no badge to wake it"). The Celebi's gym8_cleared gate protects a legendary; this is a set-piece boss at the band's edge, and a player who comes early meets a fight they may lose, and a bear no ball of theirs will hold (ursaluna.catch; the wake tells them so).
wake.awake_nbt_why: tools/legendaries.py AWAKE, the flags the Celebi's wake merges, exactly. PoseType is NOT set to another value: EXP-023 proved only "SLEEP" and principle 7 forbids guessing the rest of the enum, so RecalculatePose 1b hands the pose back to Cobblemon. NoAI and NoGravity STAY ON, as they do for the woken Celebi: the bear holds its den instead of wandering down the passage, and the fight comes to it. UNPROVEN, and the experiment's first question: that Unbattleable 0b merged onto a live entity lets a battle start (EXP-023 proved 1b blocks one), and that a NoAI Pokemon can be battled at all.
wake.start_why: the bear does NOT start the battle itself. Cobblemon 1.8.0 ships no command that starts a battle against a wild Pokemon (the jar's com/cobblemon/mod/common/command classes: no battle-start command, only SpectateBattle and StopBattle), so 'fights when you get close' is: it wakes, roars, loses its sleep flags, and the player sends out a Pokemon at it as at any wild Pokemon. A forced battle would need a mechanism nothing in this repository has proven.
wake.message: The Ursaluna stirs, and rises to face you.
wake.awake_holder_why: a score on this pack's own objective cobblers.ursaluna, the Celebi's arrangement: ursaluna_cave/wake sets it to 1, ursaluna_cave/dress sets it back to 0, and dress runs exactly when a bear is made dormant (installed, returned, or lying down again after a fight fled, ursaluna.returns.rests), so the flag cannot outlive the entity it describes. ursaluna_cave/load does NOT reset it: a restart must not put a woken bear back to sleep.

returns.status: built 2026-10-02, not run in game: experiments/EXP-049-ursaluna-wake
returns.cooldown_why: one hour of server time (72,000 ticks, three Minecraft days), on the game clock (`time query gametime`), so it runs only while the server runs and a restart neither stops nor resets it. Long enough that the fight is a place you go back to, not one you farm: the gulch's farm Megas, which exist to be farmed, return in 10 and 15 minutes (data/gulch_mine.json farm_tiers respawn_ticks 12000 and 18000); the den is four to six times slower, so an evening's session meets it two or three times between the whole group. Short enough that a friend who missed it, or a player back with six badges to catch it, finds it within a session.
returns.clear_why: it returns only with nobody within 48 blocks of its spot (the keeper's player_radius): nobody in the hall, the den or the inner part of the passage, so it never appears in front of anyone and nobody can wait it out standing in the hall; a player has to leave and come back. The den spot must still be loaded for the keeper to act (`execute if loaded`), which a player walking up from Highwire does before reaching the mouth.
returns.absent_why: the gulch Megas' rule (tools/gulch_mine.py megas/keep_*): absent on two loaded keeper passes in a row (80 ticks) before absence counts, because entities load a moment after their chunk. A pass with the den spot unloaded resets the count.
returns.signals: BEATEN: the battle_fainted callback (a wild Pokemon fainting in battle) hands the fainted Pokemon's UUID to ursaluna_cave/gone, which starts the clock (why 1) only if it is the UUID ursaluna_cave/dress stored for the bear. CAUGHT: the pokemon_captured callback, the same with why 2 (the entity is gone by then, so the UUID is the key). Both are the blackout guardians' route, which resolved a guardian beaten in battle and one caught on staging (EXP-042 session 5; tools/blackout_pack.py recovery/resolve_pid), and the UUID text is built by the same method. VANISHED: a bear absent with no callback (a sword, an arrow, /kill: Cobblemon ignores Invulnerable, EXP-023) starts the clock when its absence counts (why 3). WANDERED cannot happen: the bear has NoAI and NoGravity awake or asleep and keep puts a sleeping one back on its spot, so a tagged bear anywhere loaded IS the bear and resets the absence count; a bear not yet loaded is what absent_passes waits out; and a load race that still makes a second one is removed by keep. The first sighting starts the clock and nothing later moves it; only dress (a bear installed) clears it.
returns.rests: an awake bear still alive with nobody within clear_radius (a fight fled, not won) is dressed again: asleep, on its spot, the awake score 0. Its health is whatever the fight left: no command that heals a wild Pokemon is proven here.

catch.status: built 2026-10-02, not run in game: experiments/EXP-049-ursaluna-wake
catch.message: The Ursaluna shrugs off the ball. No trainer with fewer than six badges will hold this one.
catch.why: the owner: "catchable only late". Of the three ways asked for, (c), chosen by evidence from the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar. (a) The level cap alone needs the bear at 41 or more: the first trainer after six badges, route_07_trainer_01, tops at 41 (data/trainers.json), so a cap after gym 6 is 41 to 50 (Blaine's ace), and a level-41 bear is no fight for the 20-28 band. The fight and the catch need different levels, and one entity has one. (b) The native `uncatchable` property exists (UncatchableProperty, a FlagProperty kept in Pokemon.customProperties and read by EmptyPokeBallEntity through isCatchable), but it is one flag for every thrower, and no verified command clears it on a live entity (data/sapling_celebi.json spawn_properties_why): a late player could never catch a bear an early one had woken. (c) The level-cap pack's own hook (tools/levelcap_pack.py): the poke_ball_capture_calculated callback, after the ball's maths, in battle and out, sets the shakes to 0 (it breaks free, a Master Ball included) when the target carries the bear's tag (has_tag, EntityMoLangFunctions, which PokemonEntity's MoLang struct includes: the jar) and the thrower, asked by ursaluna_cave/catch_check through the same tag handshake, lacks a flag here. Per thrower, the fight stays at 30, and the flags are the badge advancements proven set by beating a gym (EXP-027). LATE means six of eight badges (gym6_cleared), three gyms after the den is reachable, the gate the south of the Rift already uses (the gulch zone, SOUTHERN_RIFT_MEGA.md). A sleeping bear breaks free for everyone and the ball wakes it: nobody catches the boss without meeting it. The hook is built and loads on staging but no throw has been seen (docs/STATE.md 'The level-cap trap'), so this rests on the same unproven chain as the level cap.

model.cube_bounds_source: assets/cobblemon/bedrock/pokemon/models/0901_ursaluna/ursaluna.geo.json: the union of every cube's origin and size, ignoring bone rotation (x -28..36 px, y -40.5..42 px, z -38.5..27.8 px): an over-estimate, so a chamber sized to it is safe
model.assumed: the rendered model scales with the effective scale as the hitbox does; at 2.0 the bear is about 8 wide, 8.3 long and at most 10.3 tall, with a 3.6 by 4.0 hitbox

teddiursa.why: an ACTIVATED Habitat Block (data/habitat_blocks.json, placed by tools/habitat_blocks.py with every other block, R9E) that keeps up to `group` Teddiursa alive round itself, and a Habitat pool authored in data/spawns.json (compiled by tools/compile_spawns.py). It was a natural ReplaceSpawns block until 2026-10-02, and the owner walked the slope and 'didnt see ... many teddiursa spawns': a natural block only swaps the species natural spawning happens to pick within its range, which is rare, and staging measured 0 Pokemon within 32 of it with the pool resolved. An activated block spawns its own pool and refills it as they are caught or despawn (the elder nests and Driftmouth Isle, staging 2026-09-26: 23 Fletchling round one birch). The pool is Teddiursa alone, 20-28: the_tri_peaks band (20-28 since the encounter rebuild of 2026-10-02) and below level 30, where Teddiursa evolves (Cobblemon 1.8.0 species data).

npc.at_why: 8 blocks across the axis from the mouth on the Highwire side and 4 out from it (s=-4, p=8), on the slope beside the opening, standing one above the heightmap ground (tools/ground.py: y162): the first thing a player coming from Highwire reaches, outside every carved block and every column the cave writes. Placed over RCON by spawnnpcat after a restart (tools/reapply.py's "npc" action, as R9F, R17 and R17F place theirs); the class ships in cobblers_dialogue, compiled from data/dialogue.json.
